stories.title: Pine AI getting 75.4% (SoTA) on τ³-Voice Leaderboard
stories.paragraph: Pine AI has claimed the top position on the τ³-Voice leaderboard with a score of 75.4%, which evaluates AI agents on realistic customer-service phone call scenarios. The τ-bench suite is notable for testing multi-turn, tool-using agents under conditions that simulate actual deployment rather than static question-answering. The result places Pine AI ahead of other publicly listed systems on a benchmark that has become a reference point for conversational AI agent evaluation.

stories.title: DFlash 2: Keep Drafting Parallel
stories.paragraph: Inco AI has published details on DFlash 2, a speculative decoding method designed to accelerate large language model inference by running draft generation steps in parallel. Speculative decoding works by using a smaller model to propose token sequences that a larger model then verifies in fewer forward passes, reducing latency. The DFlash 2 approach extends this by allowing multiple draft sequences to be evaluated concurrently, aiming to improve throughput on hardware setups where parallelism is available.

stories.title: AI is less likely to launch a nuclear strike when it reasons in Japanese
stories.paragraph: A study examined how language choice during chain-of-thought reasoning affects the decisions AI models make in simulated high-stakes geopolitical scenarios, including nuclear escalation. Researchers found that models prompted to reason in Japanese produced notably more cautious outputs compared to reasoning in English, suggesting that the training data distribution associated with a given language shapes the model's implicit values and risk tolerance. The finding raises questions about how multilingual models should be evaluated for safety, since behavioral properties may shift depending on which language is used at inference time.

stories.title: smolmachines / smolvm as a sandbox for untrusted Python & JavaScript
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison used Claude Fable 5 running inside Claude Code for web to research smolmachines and its smolvm component as a sandboxing option for executing untrusted Python and JavaScript. The investigation focused on whether smolvm could enforce meaningful limits on RAM and CPU time, which are the two primary resource vectors that untrusted code tends to abuse. The write-up documents both the capabilities and the current constraints of the approach, providing a practical reference for developers considering lightweight sandboxing without full container overhead.

stories.title: Don't Paste the AI, please
stories.paragraph: The site dontpastetheai.com advocates against copying AI-generated text directly into documents, codebases, or communications without review and editing. The argument centers on the observation that unreviewed AI output frequently contains errors, hallucinated facts, or stylistic inconsistencies that become embedded in downstream artifacts when pasted without scrutiny. The project appears aimed at practitioners who use AI assistants daily, encouraging a habit of treating model output as a draft rather than a finished product.

stories.title: Conceptual integrity and counting lines of code
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison published highlights from a conversation recorded for the Talking Postgres podcast with Claire Giordano, focused on how AI is changing software development practices. A central theme is conceptual integrity — the idea, originally articulated by Fred Brooks, that coherent systems require a unified vision — and how AI-assisted coding affects a developer's ability to maintain that integrity across a growing codebase. Willison used Claude to lightly edit the transcript for readability, noting that lines-of-code counts become a less meaningful metric when AI can generate large volumes of code quickly.

stories.title: Quoting Jeremy Morrell
stories.paragraph: Simon Willison quoted Jeremy Morrell's hypothesis that LLMs and modern browser sandbox primitives together create a new opportunity for extensible web software. Morrell's argument is that LLMs dramatically reduce the cost of writing extensions, while sandboxing technologies provide the security boundaries needed to deploy user-authored code safely. The framing positions this combination as a path toward applications with a stable, accountable core that users can extend without requiring the application vendor to anticipate every use case.

stories.title: Technical leaders should have the largest AI exhaust
stories.paragraph: A post on schipper.ai argues that technical leaders — engineering managers, principal engineers, and architects — should be among the heaviest users of AI tools within their organizations, producing the most visible trail of AI-assisted work. The author uses the term "AI exhaust" to describe the artifacts and outputs generated through AI-assisted workflows, and contends that leaders who generate significant exhaust signal to their teams that such tools are legitimate and worth investing time in learning. The piece is directed at organizations where AI adoption is inconsistent, suggesting that leadership modeling behavior is more effective than policy mandates.

stories.title: Flock Has a Powerful New AI Tool for Police. We Got Its Code
stories.paragraph: Wired obtained the source code for Flock Safety's AI-powered investigative platform, which aggregates license plate reader data, surveillance footage, and other law enforcement datasets into a unified search interface for police departments. The tool, called Flock OS Investigate, allows officers to query across multiple data sources simultaneously, raising questions about oversight and the scope of automated surveillance it enables. Flock Safety's license plate readers are already deployed in thousands of jurisdictions across the United States, making the capabilities of the connected software layer a matter of significant public interest.

stories.title: PINE64 halts their open-source hardware manufacturing until the AI bubble bursts
stories.paragraph: PINE64, the maker of low-cost Linux single-board computers including the PinePhone and Pinebook, announced it is pausing hardware manufacturing, citing the distorting effect of AI investment on the component supply chain and pricing. The company stated it will resume production once what it describes as the AI bubble deflates and component costs normalize. PINE64 has been a notable supplier to the open-source hardware community, and the pause affects a range of devices that have no direct commercial equivalents from larger manufacturers.

stories.title: Japan to require AI firms to disclose training data
stories.paragraph: Japan's government announced plans to require AI companies operating in the country to disclose information about the datasets used to train their models. The policy is aimed at improving transparency around copyright compliance and potential data biases, and follows similar regulatory discussions in the European Union. Japan had previously taken a relatively permissive stance on AI training data and copyright, making this shift a notable change in the country's regulatory posture toward the AI industry.

stories.title: New AirPods leak reveals built-in cameras and Visual Intelligence
stories.paragraph: Leaked information suggests that an upcoming AirPods model from Apple will include built-in infrared cameras intended to support the company's Visual Intelligence feature, which uses on-device and server-side AI to analyze the user's environment. Visual Intelligence was introduced with the iPhone 16 line and uses the camera to identify objects, text, and locations in real time. If accurate, integrating cameras into AirPods would extend the feature to a hands-free form factor, though the leak does not specify a release timeline or the exact camera specifications.

stories.title: OpenAI 'will be a public company in 2027' or sooner, CFO Friar tells employees
stories.paragraph: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar told employees the company expects to go public by 2027 or earlier, according to CNBC. The statement is notable given OpenAI's ongoing corporate restructuring from a capped-profit to a for-profit entity, a transition that has been a prerequisite for any public offering. No specific exchange or valuation target was disclosed in the employee communication.

stories.title: AI was supposed to win people over by now – it hasn't
stories.paragraph: A TechCrunch analysis argues that despite years of high-profile AI product launches, mainstream consumer enthusiasm for AI tools has not materialized at the scale the industry anticipated by 2026. The piece points to persistent concerns about reliability, privacy, and practical utility as factors dampening adoption. It serves as a counterpoint to the widespread industry narrative that AI would rapidly become indispensable to everyday users.

stories.title: Two 2030 AMD racks are expected to deliver same compute as 570 racks in 2024
stories.paragraph: AMD published a progress report stating it is tracking ahead of its rack-scale AI energy efficiency goal, with two projected 2030-generation racks expected to deliver the same compute output as 570 comparable racks from 2024. The claim reflects a roughly 285x improvement in compute-per-rack efficiency over six years. AMD frames this as progress toward a previously stated target of a 30x improvement in energy efficiency for AI training and inference by 2025, a goal it says it has already exceeded.

stories.title: Offering Zero Data Retention for frontier models
stories.paragraph: OpenAI reaffirmed its Zero Data Retention (ZDR) option for eligible API customers, meaning inputs and outputs are not stored after a request completes. The company also previewed a feature called Private Safety Processing, which is designed to run AI safety checks without retaining or exposing user data. The combination addresses a tension that enterprise customers have raised: how to use advanced safety monitoring while maintaining strict data-handling commitments.

stories.title: Daily Reminder to Not Listen to Google's AI Overview
stories.paragraph: Author John Scalzi published a post urging readers to treat Google's AI Overview feature with skepticism, citing specific instances where the feature produced inaccurate or misleading summaries at the top of search results. The post is part of a recurring series, suggesting the accuracy concerns have persisted rather than been resolved with product updates. It joins a broader public conversation about the risks of surfacing AI-generated summaries as the first thing users see in search.

stories.title: 5 new ways to level up your learning with Search
stories.paragraph: Google published a back-to-school post outlining five AI-assisted study features available in Search, including integrations with NotebookLM that allow users to add search results directly to a notebook via an 'Add Notebook' button. The post targets students returning to school and highlights the ability to ask follow-up questions within Search using an 'Ask Google' prompt. The update positions Google Search as a study workflow tool alongside its existing AI Overview and Gemini-powered features.

stories.title: Unsloth Dynamic 3.0 GGUFs
stories.paragraph: Unsloth released Dynamic 3.0 GGUFs, an updated quantization format for large language models designed to preserve model quality at lower bit depths by applying non-uniform quantization across layers. The approach selectively assigns higher precision to layers deemed more sensitive to quantization error, rather than applying a single bit-width uniformly. This is notable for practitioners running inference locally, as it offers a way to reduce model size while minimizing accuracy degradation compared to standard GGUF quantization.

stories.title: SPADE: Self-Play in Adaptive Synthetic Executable Environments
stories.paragraph: Researchers introduced SPADE, a self-play reinforcement learning framework in which a single large language model acts as both environment generator and agent, continuously creating new goals as the learner's capability improves. The framework addresses a known limitation of existing training setups, where hand-curated or statically synthesized task pools fix the difficulty distribution and cannot adapt to a more capable model. By generating executable synthetic environments with verifiable outcomes, SPADE enables open-ended skill acquisition without relying on frozen verifiers or human-designed curricula.

stories.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning
stories.paragraph: ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework for teaching dexterous manipulation to high-degree-of-freedom robot hands, using raw visuo-tactile perception rather than engineered state representations. The method first pretrains a policy on a generic object reposing task to build general motor skills, then applies post-training to adapt that policy to specific downstream tasks. The sim-to-real transfer approach targets long-horizon manipulation tasks, a domain where most prior RL methods have required privileged simulation state inputs.

stories.title: Beyond Teacher Likelihood: Group-Calibrated On-Policy Distillation for Long-Context Reasoning
stories.paragraph: This paper identifies a failure mode in on-policy distillation (OPD) for long-context reasoning tasks, where token-level guidance from a teacher model can favor locally fluent responses that nonetheless violate global constraints or miss evidence spread across a long input. The authors propose group-calibrated on-policy distillation, which combines dense teacher signals with response-level verification to correct for this bias. The method is motivated by the observation that task-specific verifiers and teacher likelihoods capture complementary aspects of response quality that neither approach captures alone.

stories.title: Finetuning Strategies for Querying Sounds by Vocal Imitation
stories.paragraph: This technical report describes the winning submission to the AES AIMLA 2025 Challenge on sound-effect retrieval via vocal imitation, a task where users hum or vocalize to locate matching audio. The team tested two fine-tuning strategies: contrastive learning with a frozen CED encoder, and joint contrastive-triplet learning using semi-hard negatives with a MobileNetV3 encoder. The updated report includes additional experimental details added after the competition for reproducibility.

stories.title: Lévy Attention: Single-Pass Predictive Uncertainty for Continuous-Time Attention
stories.paragraph: Researchers propose Lévy Attention, an attention mechanism for irregularly-sampled time series that produces calibrated uncertainty estimates at arbitrary continuous timestamps within a single forward pass, with no additional computational cost at inference time. The method replaces standard attention with a stochastic formulation based on Lévy processes, which yields closed-form uncertainty alongside each prediction. This is notable for applications such as medical monitoring or sensor data, where time series observations arrive at irregular intervals and trustworthiness of model outputs varies depending on how far a query timestamp falls from observed data.

stories.title: Learned, Then Lost: A Measured Single-Example Counterfactual in Pre-training
stories.paragraph: Researchers conducted a controlled experiment to directly measure, rather than estimate, the causal effect of a single training example on a finished language model. The study trained 32 GPT-2 models at 124 million parameters from scratch on OpenWebText across four conditions and eight random seeds, running the costly counterfactual comparison 24 times. The experimental design isolates the contribution of one data point by differing two full pre-training runs by only a single row in a single batch, an approach rarely attempted due to its computational expense. Results were observed at step 200 of a 9,536-step training run, providing early-stage evidence of how individual examples shape model behavior.
